title: Testing, sanitizers and undefined behaviour

objectives.text: Design boundary/reference/property tests whose checks survive release NDEBUG, keep unsafe operations out of rejection tests and distinguish observed pass from all-input proof.
Reproduce a scoped instrumented build and interpret compiler/test/sanitizer diagnostics without treating a clean run as absence of every memory, business or concurrency error.

blocks.markdown: A test is an executable claim about a declared contract, source revision, toolchain and input. Use examples for understandable behavior, boundary cases for branch/range transitions, an independently derived reference for answers and metamorphic properties for related inputs. None alone proves every possible input is correct. A property can pass for the wrong implementation: returning 0 for all additions is commutative, so add independent value/identity checks. Mutation, error status and output formatting are observable parts of the contract, not optional afterthoughts.

C assert and C++ assert macros can be disabled when NDEBUG is defined at inclusion. Do not put necessary validation, state changes or the only acceptance-test failure check inside assert. static_assert checks compile-time predicates; it cannot inspect arbitrary runtime input. Here tests use explicit conditionals/nonzero returns so the checks stay active with -DNDEBUG. Invalid input tests must verify rejection WITHOUT first performing the very overflowing/dangling/out-of-range operation being rejected.

blocks.caption: Expected output: boundary checks passed, exit 0. maximum+1 is never evaluated: the helper compares 1 with maximum-maximum first. Negative inputs short-circuit before the guarded subtraction where relevant. Run normal and -DNDEBUG builds to confirm these explicit checks are still present; that does not establish every possible arithmetic input or an actual app runtime.

blocks.markdown: The next small grid checks symmetry and the inverse relation(add(a,b)-a==b)where the accepted sums and subtraction are bounded/safe. It is derived testing evidence, not a second independent addition algorithm. Compare wider cases to a genuinely independent arbitrary-precision reference, and separately verify rejection/zero semantics at the type boundaries. A test harness can have its own bug; inspect it and test that it actually fails on a controlled wrong RESULT implementation without injecting undefined behavior.

blocks.caption: Expected output: 10201 property cases passed, exit 0. The grid is 0..100 in both arguments and every correct sum is at most 200. A fake implementation returning 0 would fail the inverse relation as soon as b > 0. Passing this finite grid is not a proof for all long long values; the pre-operation range argument and separate max boundary tests address a different part of the reasoning.

blocks.markdown: For a compatible GCC installation, an instrumented local build can use `g++ -std=c++20 -O1 -g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all lesson.cpp -o checked`, then `./checked`. Compile AND link with the driver flags so sanitizer runtimes are linked. Keep the normal strict-warning build too. Exact option support, diagnostic text and runtime availability depend on compiler/target/environment; a failed runtime setup is not a passed sanitizer check or automatically a learner-code bug. Record the actual flags, source hash, exit status, stdout/stderr and test input.

AddressSanitizer instruments classes of invalid memory access such as out-of-bounds and use-after-free; UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer instruments selected undefined operations such as some signed overflow, null/alignment and shift errors. Enabled groups differ by compiler/version; do not copy a Clang-only flag into GCC and claim equivalent coverage. A clean instrumented run covers executed instrumented paths, not unexecuted branches, all allocators/libraries, all concurrency errors, semantic units, source authenticity or profitability. Ordinary unsigned modular arithmetic can be defined yet wrong for the business contract.

When a real report appears, preserve compiler/version/mode, input, source/stack location and full first relevant diagnostic; distinguish runtime setup failures from a source violation. Reduce to the smallest reproducer without deleting the failing contract, trace ownership/range, fix the cause, then rerun the reproducer and regression/reference tests. Do not suppress sanitizer output, disable the failing check, rely on a later plausible output or claim a randomized memory-layout rerun disproved the original issue. This lesson does not execute an intentionally undefined program as a teaching demonstration.

Independent transfer: add safe subtraction/multiplication test boundaries without evaluating an overflowing expected result. Compare with Python unbounded integer arithmetic under a declared source interface. Run explicit tests with/without NDEBUG and, if available, compatible instrumented flags. Introduce a controlled defined wrong result such as always returning 0 and show the test harness exits nonzero, then restore correct source. Keep actual execution evidence separate from app-runner qualification.

Sources: [GCC instrumentation](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Instrumentation-Options.html), [assert/NDEBUG](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/error/assert.html), [Clang ASan scope](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/AddressSanitizer.html), and [Clang UBSan groups](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer.html). Clang documentation supplies conceptual comparison, not a claim that Clang or its flags were executed locally.

summary: Tests need independent answers and active failure checks, not only a green output or an assert compiled away. Sanitizers diagnose selected executed operations; preserve real diagnostics and toolchain scope, fix causes, and never promote a clean local run into universal or app-runtime safety.
